**[Category: Water]**

**Overview**
The **Lake of Dragons**, more formally known as the **Dragonmere**, is the vast, westernmost arm of the Sea of Fallen Stars. A vital freshwater-to-brackish waterway, it serves as the primary aquatic thoroughfare for the influential nations of Cormyr and Sembia, connecting the Western Heartlands to the trade routes of the wider Inner Sea.

**Geography and Hydrology**
The lake spans approximately 100 miles at its widest point, tapering eastward to a narrow channel known as "The Neck" (roughly 10 miles across) between the metropolis of Westgate and the Sembian port of Urmlaspyr. To the north, its waves lap against the rocky shores of Cormyr and the fertile lowlands of Sembia. To the south lies the rugged, lawless region known as the Dragon Coast.

While technically an inlet of the Sea of Fallen Stars, the Dragonmere possesses a distinct hydrological character. It is fed by several major rivers—most notably the **Starwater River** flowing from the Storm Horns through Marsember, and the **Tun River** which drains the marshlands to the west. Consequently, the water in the western Dragonmere is largely fresh, becoming increasingly brackish and salty as it flows eastward through the Neck into the main body of the Inner Sea.

**Political and Economic Significance**
The Lake of Dragons is one of the busiest shipping lanes in all of Faerûn. It is the lifeblood of **Cormyr**, the Forest Kingdom; the royal capital, **Suzail**, and the City of Spices, **Marsember**, both boast massive fortified harbors on its northern banks. Merchant cogs constantly traverse the waters, ferrying timber, grain, and spices to the wealthy markets of Sembia and beyond.

The southern shore stands in stark contrast to the regimented north. Here lie the independent city-states of the Dragon Coast—**Teziir**, **Elversult** (inland), and the infamous **Westgate**. These ports are havens for independent merchant guilds and, frequently, smugglers looking to bypass Cormyrean tariffs.

**Ecological and Submerged Lore**
Beneath the surface, the Lake of Dragons is far from empty. The depths house **Naramyr**, a reclusive kingdom of sea elves (alu-tel'quessir). The Naramyr elves maintain a tentative pact with the surface dwellers, particularly Cormyr, often aiding sailors shipwrecked by the lake's notorious sudden storms.

The name "Lake of Dragons" is derived not only from its proximity to the Dragon Coast but also from the terrifying marine life that stalks its currents. **Dragon turtles** are known to dwell in the deeper trenches, occasionally rising to exact tribute from passing ships. Furthermore, legends persist of ancient aquatic dragons slumbering in the silt, remnants of the Time of Dragons when the wyrms ruled the skies and seas alike.

**Hazards**
Beyond monsters, the lake is known for its treacherous weather. Fierce squalls can descend from the Storm Horns with little warning, whipping the shallow waters into a frenzy. Additionally, despite the naval power of Cormyr, piracy remains a constant threat, with corsairs from the Pirate Isles often slipping through the Neck to prey on fat merchant carracks before retreating to the lawless harbors of the south.
